今天的主题：城市噪音、城市生活和环境。这组词对 G 类特别实用：写作 Task 2 常考「城市生活的利弊」「政府该怎样减少城市噪音和污染」；小作文投诉信最常见的就是给邻居或市政写信抱怨噪音和交通；口语 Part 1 的 Hometown、Noise，Part 3 的 urban life 都能直接用。

例句

  • Many urban residents complain about noise from traffic and building work.（很多城市居民抱怨交通和施工带来的噪音。）
  • The council needs to tackle congestion in the city centre.（市政府需要解决市中心的交通拥堵。）
  • Long-term exposure to loud noise can disturb people's sleep and harm their health.（长期暴露在大噪音中会干扰睡眠、损害健康。）
  • After moving to the countryside, I found it hard to cope with the busy city again.（搬到乡下以后，我发现再回到繁忙的城市很难适应。）
  • Governments should invest more in public transport infrastructure to reduce the number of private vehicles.（政府应该加大对公共交通基础设施的投入，减少私家车数量。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 noise、resident、tackle 写一句你对城市噪音的看法，大作文和投诉信都能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Making cities feel quieter（让城市感觉更安静）。这集讲城市噪音有多伤人，一位孟买人在国外住了 12 年回国后受不了家乡的吵闹，还有加拿大蒙特利尔的声音艺术家把会「唱歌」的沙子和海浪声放进公园，反而让公园感觉更安静。提到的东京声景也和你在日本的生活有关。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：耳语大概是多少分贝？a) 3 b) 13 c) 30。顺便听出：孟买白天的噪音经常达到多少分贝？到 2050 年大约多少人会有听力损失？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Chhavi Sachdev 和 Charles Montambault 两段是真实录音，口音不同、语速稍快，多听几遍。
  4. 第三遍挑 Chhavi 那段（"I mean, India in general is just really loud..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：decibel（分贝）、dress loud（穿得张扬）、can't handle something（受不了，应付不了）、art installation（艺术装置）、squeaky（吱吱响的）、counterintuitive（反直觉的）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Georgie：And I'm Georgie. Neil, I'm going to play you two sound recordings录音, and I want you to tell me how you feel when you hear them.

Georgie：我是乔治。尼尔，我要给你放两段录音，你告诉我听的时候有什么感觉。

Neil：OK.

Neil：好的。

Georgie：First this… And now this.

Georgie：先听这段……再听这段。

Neil：Oh, well, that first clip片段 made me feel really relaxed. But the second one – oh, it's horrible! I felt quite stressed out压力很大，很紧张 actually.

Neil：哦，第一段让我觉得特别放松。可第二段，哎呀，太难听了！说实话我觉得挺紧张的。

Georgie：Oh no! Well, this little experiment shows how much we are affected by the noise around us. And that's a problem if you're one of the four billion people around the world who live in cities.

Georgie：哎呀！这个小实验说明我们受周围噪音的影响有多大。如果你是全世界住在城市里的四十亿人之一，这就是个问题了。

Neil：Yes, whether it's the rattle咔嗒声 of train tracks, honking按喇叭 car horns汽车喇叭, or the roar轰鸣 of aeroplanes overhead在头顶上, modern cities are full of noise and this can have serious effects. The World Health Organisation reports that by 2050, around 2.5 billion people will experience hearing loss听力损失, and exposure暴露，接触 to loud noise has been linked to与……有关 stress and anxiety焦虑.

Neil：是啊，不管是火车轨道的咔嗒声、汽车喇叭的鸣笛声，还是头顶飞机的轰鸣声，现代城市到处都是噪音，而且影响可能很严重。世界卫生组织报告说，到 2050 年，大约 25 亿人会有听力损失，而长期处在大噪音里还和压力、焦虑有关。

Georgie：In this episode, we'll be hearing about ways to make our cities quieter, more relaxing places, using some useful new words and phrases. And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary along with a quiz and worksheet练习题 on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Georgie：这一集我们会聊聊怎样让城市更安静、更让人放松，同时学一些有用的新词和短语。别忘了，所有词汇以及小测验和练习题都在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上。

Neil：But now I have a question for you, Georgie. Sound is measured in units called decibels分贝. But how many decibels分贝 would it be if I whispered耳语，低声说? A whisper耳语，低声说 is speaking like this. Is it: a) 3 decibels分贝, b) 13 decibels分贝, or c) 30 decibels分贝?

Neil：不过现在我先问你个问题，乔治。声音的计量单位叫分贝。如果我小声耳语，大概是多少分贝？耳语就是像这样说话。是 a) 3 分贝，b) 13 分贝，还是 c) 30 分贝？

Georgie：Oh, that's really hard. I'll go for b) 13 decibels分贝.

Georgie：哦，这个好难。我选 b) 13 分贝。

Neil：Well, we'll find out弄清楚，得知 the answer at the end of the programme. Let's start in one of the noisiest cities in the world – Mumbai in India, where daytime noise levels regularly hit 80 decibels分贝, which is over 20 decibels分贝 higher than World Health Organisation recommendations. Listen to Mumbai native本地人 Chhavi Sachdev share her experiences of living in this noisy city with BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World.

Neil：好，节目最后揭晓答案。我们先从世界上最吵的城市之一说起，印度孟买。那里白天的噪音经常达到 80 分贝，比世界卫生组织的建议值高出 20 多分贝。来听听土生土长的孟买人查薇·萨奇德夫在 BBC 国际频道节目《改变世界的人》里讲她在这座嘈杂城市生活的经历。

Chhavi Sachdev：I mean, India in general is just really loud. We are a loud people. We dress loud穿得张扬, we talk loud, we celebrate loud, we watch movies loud. When people ask me what I miss about living abroad在国外, I tell them it's the quiet, because after 12 years of living in the US and Europe, when I got back, I realised I couldn't handle it anymore. I'd gotten used to习惯了 lower levels of noise.

Chhavi Sachdev：我是说，印度整体上就是特别吵。我们是一个很吵的民族。穿得张扬，说话大声，庆祝大声，看电影也开很大声。别人问我怀念国外生活的什么，我说是安静。因为在美国和欧洲住了 12 年，回来以后我发现自己已经受不了了。我已经习惯了更低的噪音。

Georgie：Chhavi says, "Indians talk loud, celebrate loud and dress loud穿得张扬." To dress loud穿得张扬 means to wear clothes with bright colours and large, bold patterns醒目的图案.

Georgie：查薇说「印度人说话大声、庆祝大声、穿得也张扬」。dress loud 的意思是穿颜色鲜艳、图案又大又醒目的衣服。

Neil：When Chhavi returned to India after living overseas在海外, she says she couldn't handle the noise. If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal or cope with应付，处理.

Neil：查薇在国外生活后回到印度，她说自己受不了那种噪音。can't handle something 就是觉得某事很难应付、很难承受。

Georgie：So, what can be done to tackle处理，解决 noise in cities like Mumbai? One interesting approach involves using sound itself to make things feel quieter. Soundscaping声景（设计） is the idea of adding certain sounds to busy public spaces so that they sound and feel more relaxing.

Georgie：那么，像孟买这样的城市能怎么解决噪音问题呢？有一个很有意思的办法，就是用声音本身让环境感觉更安静。声景设计（soundscaping）就是往热闹的公共场所里加入某些声音，让那里听起来、感觉起来更放松。

Neil：Sound artist Charles Montambault lives near the Parc des Madelinots, a busy city park in Montreal, Canada. Charles was inspired to recreate重现 the ocean sounds he heard on holiday in the Magdalen Islands in his city park back home. On BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World, he tells reporter Natasha Fernandes that these sounds included ocean waves and some unusual-sounding sand.

Neil：声音艺术家查尔斯·蒙坦博住在加拿大蒙特利尔一个热闹的城市公园马德里诺公园附近。他在马格达伦群岛度假时听到了大海的声音，受到启发，想在家门口的城市公园里重现这些声音。他在 BBC 国际频道节目《改变世界的人》里告诉记者娜塔莎·费尔南德斯，这些声音包括海浪声，还有一种声音很奇特的沙子。

Charles Montambault：The sand on the Magdalen Islands can sing. When you walk into the sand firmly用力地, the sand makes some squeaky吱吱响的 sounds, so that's one sound that is kind of funny, kind of special.

Charles Montambault：马格达伦群岛的沙子会唱歌。你用力踩在沙子上，沙子会发出吱吱的声音，这种声音有点好玩，也有点特别。

Natasha Fernandes：Inside the small park, surrounded by busy roads, Charles and his team set up an immersive沉浸式的 sound art installation艺术装置 in the form of speakers planted in flower beds花坛.

Natasha Fernandes：在这个被繁忙道路包围的小公园里，查尔斯和团队搭了一个沉浸式的声音艺术装置，就是把音箱藏在花坛里。

Charles Montambault：So, the art installation艺术装置 was really to make this park a little quieter by adding some quiet noises. So, it's counterintuitive反直觉的, but you can make a park less noisy by adding some calmer sounds.

Charles Montambault：这个艺术装置其实就是想通过加一些安静的声音，让公园稍微安静一点。这有点反直觉，但加一些更平静的声音，确实能让公园没那么吵。

Georgie：The sand on the Magdalen Islands is squeaky吱吱响的 – it makes a high-pitched尖声的，高音的 sound called a squeak吱吱声 when stepped on. Charles played recordings录音 of this sand, ocean waves and other relaxing sounds through speakers hidden in the park. He created an art installation艺术装置 – a work of art designed to give people an interactive互动的 experience.

Georgie：马格达伦群岛的沙子是 squeaky 的，踩上去会发出一种尖细的声音，叫 squeak。查尔斯通过藏在公园里的音箱播放这种沙子、海浪和其他让人放松的声音的录音。他创作了一个艺术装置，也就是一件为了给人互动体验而设计的艺术作品。

Neil：By adding more relaxing sounds, Charles' art installation艺术装置 actually made the park feel quieter. It's an example of something that's counterintuitive反直觉的, meaning it happens differently from how you would expect.

Neil：通过加入更多放松的声音，查尔斯的艺术装置反而让公园感觉更安静了。这就是 counterintuitive（反直觉）的例子，意思是事情的结果和你预想的不一样。

Georgie：What a great idea! And similar soundscapes声景（设计） are now helping city dwellers城市居民 relax in other cities too, including Tokyo and Barcelona. Now Neil, you asked me a question about a very quiet sound – a whisper耳语，低声说. So, are you going to reveal揭晓 the correct answer?

Georgie：好主意！类似的声景现在也在帮助其他城市的居民放松，包括东京和巴塞罗那。好了尼尔，你问过我一个关于很小的声音，也就是耳语的问题。现在要公布正确答案了吗？

Neil：I asked you how loud a whisper耳语，低声说 is.

Neil：我问你耳语有多大声。

Georgie：Yes, and I said 13 decibels分贝.

Georgie：对，我说 13 分贝。

Neil：Well, 13 is an unlucky number and you are wrong.

Neil：嗯，13 是个不吉利的数字，你答错了。

Georgie：Ah!

Georgie：啊！

Neil：It was actually 30. OK. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with decibel分贝 – the unit for measuring sound.

Neil：其实是 30 分贝。好，我们来回顾一下学过的词，先是 decibel，分贝，测量声音的单位。

Georgie：Someone who dresses loud穿得张扬 likes to wear clothes with bright colours and bold designs.

Georgie：dresses loud 的人喜欢穿颜色鲜艳、设计醒目的衣服。

Neil：If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal with.

Neil：can't handle something 就是觉得某事很难应付。

Georgie：An art installation艺术装置 is an artwork designed to create an interactive互动的 experience in a certain space.

Georgie：art installation（艺术装置）是在特定空间里创造互动体验的艺术作品。

Neil：The adjective squeaky吱吱响的 describes things which make a high-pitched尖声的，高音的 sound like a mouse.

Neil：形容词 squeaky 形容东西发出像老鼠叫一样尖细的声音。

Georgie：Squeak吱吱声, squeak吱吱声! And finally, if you call something counterintuitive反直觉的, you mean it happens differently from how you would expect. Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to hear more about this and many other trending topics, you'll find more episodes and learning activities on our website, bbclearningenglish.com. See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.

Georgie：吱吱！最后，如果你说某事 counterintuitive，意思是它的结果和你预想的不一样。我们的六分钟又到了。如果你想听更多这类话题和其他热门话题，我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有更多节目和学习活动。下次见，再见啦。

Neil：再见……！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（噪音的危害、孟买的例子、蒙特利尔公园怎么用声音让公园变安静），6 个表达都知道意思，Chhavi 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. Sound is measured in units called ______.（分贝）
  2. My grandmother likes to dress ______ in bright red and yellow.（张扬）
  3. I moved out of the city because I couldn't ______ the noise any more.（受不了）
  4. The old door is really ______; it makes a noise every time you open it.（吱吱响的）
  5. It sounds ______, but adding sounds can make a park feel quieter.（反直觉的）
  6. Heavy traffic and ______ are big problems in most capital cities.（拥堵）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，30 分贝。乔治猜的是 13，猜错了。孟买白天的噪音经常达到 80 分贝，比世卫组织建议值高 20 多分贝；到 2050 年大约 25 亿人会有听力损失。填空：1. decibels 2. loud 3. handle 4. squeaky 5. counterintuitive 6. congestion

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：What can governments do to make cities quieter? 用英语说两三句：I think the government should ... / For example, they could ...。也可以想想：东京算吵还是安静？你住的地方最大的噪音来源是什么？
